sec-01-c2.text: Microsoft (2017). Threats - Microsoft Threat Modeling Tool. Microsoft Learn.
sec-01-c2.quote: Microsoft uses the STRIDE model, which categorizes different types of threats and simplifies the overall security conversations.
sec-01-c2.claim: The STRIDE framework (Microsoft) lists categories of threats: Spoofing identity, Tampering with data, Repudiation, Information disclosure, Denial of service, Elevation of privilege.

sec-02-c1.text: SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet. OWASP Cheat Sheet Series.
sec-02-c1.quote: Define the SQL structure separately from its data values, then bind those values through the database API. Prepared statements treat bound values as data rather than SQL syntax.
sec-02-c1.claim: The fix is parameterized queries: SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = ?, with the value passed separately.

sec-02-c2.quote: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks are a type of injection, in which malicious scripts are injected into otherwise benign and trusted websites.
sec-02-c2.claim: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) happens when user input is reflected unescaped into HTML, letting an attacker inject JavaScript that runs in another user's browser.

sec-02-c3.text: (2025). A01:2025 Broken Access Control. OWASP Top 10:2025.
sec-02-c3.quote: Maintaining its position at #1 in the Top Ten, 100% of the applications tested were found to have some form of broken access control.
sec-02-c3.claim: The OWASP Top 10's #1 risk for years running is Broken Access Control.

sec-03-c1.text: Password Storage Cheat Sheet. OWASP Cheat Sheet Series.
sec-03-c1.quote: Fast hashing algorithms such as SHA-256 are not suitable for password storage because they allow attackers to perform large numbers of guesses quickly.
sec-03-c1.claim: Storing a simple hash (MD5, SHA-1, even SHA-256) isn't enough.

sec-03-c1.text: Password Storage Cheat Sheet. OWASP Cheat Sheet Series.
sec-03-c1.quote: A unique salt must be added to each password to prevent attackers from using precomputed lookup tables like rainbow tables.
sec-03-c1.claim: Each password gets a unique random salt stored alongside the hash, defeating rainbow tables.

sec-03-c3.text: M. Jones, J. Bradley, N. Sakimura (2015). RFC 7519: JSON Web Token (JWT). RFC Editor (IETF).
sec-03-c3.quote: JSON Web Token (JWT) is a compact, URL-safe means of representing claims to be transferred between two parties.
sec-03-c3.claim: JWT (JSON Web Tokens) take a different approach: pack the user info into a signed token and let the client carry it.

sec-03-c3.text: N. Sakimura, J. Bradley, M. Jones, B. de Medeiros, C. Mortimore (2023). OpenID Connect Core 1.0 incorporating errata set 2. OpenID Foundation.
sec-03-c3.quote: OpenID Connect 1.0 is a simple identity layer on top of the OAuth 2.0 protocol. It enables Clients to verify the identity of the End-User based on the authentication performed by an Authorization Server
sec-03-c3.claim: "Sign in with Google" works because Google issues a token to the third-party app proving you logged in to Google.

sec-04-c2.text: Hash Functions. NIST Computer Security Resource Center.
sec-04-c2.quote: A hash algorithm is used to map a message of arbitrary length to a fixed-length message digest.
sec-04-c2.claim: A cryptographic hash function maps arbitrary input to a fixed-size output (e.g., 256 bits).

sec-04-c2.text: Chad Boutin (2022). NIST Retires SHA-1 Cryptographic Algorithm. National Institute of Standards and Technology.
sec-04-c2.quote: Today’s more powerful computers can create fraudulent messages that result in the same hash as the original, potentially compromising the authentic message. These “collision” attacks have been used to undermine SHA-1 in recent years.
sec-04-c2.claim: MD5 and SHA-1 are broken: collisions can be generated cheaply, so they should not be used for security purposes (signatures, certs).

sec-05-c2.text: (2021). Understanding Denial-of-Service Attacks. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA).
sec-05-c2.quote: A denial-of-service (DoS) attack occurs when legitimate users are unable to access information systems, devices, or other network resources due to the actions of a malicious cyber threat actor.
sec-05-c2.claim: A Denial-of-Service (DoS) attack overwhelms a target so legitimate users can't reach it.

sec-05-c2.text: (2021). Understanding Denial-of-Service Attacks. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA).
sec-05-c2.quote: A distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack occurs when multiple machines are operating together to attack one target.
sec-05-c2.claim: Distributed DoS (DDoS) uses thousands of compromised devices (botnets) to amplify the assault.

sec-05-c3.text: Vulnerability Disclosure Policy. Google Project Zero.
sec-05-c3.quote: Project Zero follows a 90+30 disclosure deadline policy, which means that a vendor has 90 days after Project Zero notifies them about a security vulnerability to make a patch available to users.
sec-05-c3.claim: Coordinated disclosure sets a deadline, typically 90 days, after which the researcher may publish to incentivize timely fixes.

sec-03-c2.text: (2025). NIST Special Publication 800-63B: Authentication and Authenticator Management. National Institute of Standards and Technology.
sec-03-c2.quote: The physical authenticator then serves as “something you have,” while the biometric match serves as “something you are.”
sec-03-c2.claim: Factors come from three categories: something you know (password, PIN), something you have (phone, hardware token), something you are (fingerprint, face).

sec-04-c1.text: National Institute of Standards and Technology (2001). FIPS 197, Advanced Encryption Standard (AES). NIST Computer Security Resource Center.
sec-04-c1.quote: In 2000, NIST announced the selection of the Rijndael block cipher family as the winner of the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) competition.
sec-04-c1.claim: AES is the standard symmetric cipher.
